messages:
raj: heads-up — saw a spike of Pending pods on gpu-mixed pools in us-west-2 around 06:10. autoscaler spun an on-demand node, but most GPU pods stayed pending because of taints/tolerations mismatch.

emma: which taint was blocking them? any driver errors on the nodes?

raj: ran a quick check: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-mixed -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.spec.taints}{"\\n"}{end}'` -> new nodes came up with `{"name":"interruptible","value":"spot","effect":"NoSchedule"}` and a custom taint `gpu-ready=false:NoSchedule` while the node-init job hadn't finished installing drivers. scheduler refused to place pods even though autoscaler satisfied capacity.

kai: we have topology spread constraints that prefer cross-zone scheduling. the new on-demand was only in us-west-2a and a bunch of pods had `topology.kubernetes.io/zone: us-west-2b` affinity, so they were effectively unschedulable even with capacity.

dani: propose two changes: 1) add a pre-schedulable probe in node-init that only removes `gpu-ready=false:NoSchedule` after driver + nvidia-device-plugin are healthy, and 2) change autoscaler to prefer warm-standby spot nodes per-zone (warmspare) and only allow on-demand scale-up when queue depth > threshold. also add a soft-evict mode for low-priority pods.

raj: +1. example lifecycle snippet for node-init PK:

```
# DaemonSet: node-probe-init (pseudocode)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-probe-init
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: driver-check
        image: infra/node-init:stable
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/wait-for-driver && kubectl patch node $NODE_NAME -p '{\"spec\":{\"taints\":[]}}'"]
```

Note: the patch should remove only the `gpu-ready=false:NoSchedule` taint, keep `interruptible=spot:NoSchedule`.

emma: cost impact concerns — adding more on-demand will blow monthly GPU spend. can we tune autoscaler scoring to prefer spot warmspare with a short warmup?

kai: quick math: avg spot GPU ~ $0.30/hr, on-demand ~ $2.10/hr (~7x). If we maintain 1 warmspare GPU per zone (idle) vs spinning on-demand for 5-minute bursts, warmspare wins once burst frequency > ~2/day per zone.

dani: autoscaler policy proposal (high-level):
- targetWarmSparePerZone: 1-2 GPUs
- onDemandScaleTrigger: pendingPods > 4 for > 120s OR queue growth rate > 0.2/s
- preemptibleFallbackOrder: spot-same-zone -> spot-other-zone -> on-demand
- tolerateLabel: `interruptibility=soft` for background jobs

raj: also add a toleration pattern: latency-sensitive pods get `tolerations: []` (no spot toleration), best-effort batch gets `tolerations: [{key: \"interruptible\", operator: \"Exists\", effect: \"PreferNoSchedule\"}]`. Use node affinity to prefer zones where warmspares exist.

emma: I pushed a small dashboard patch to show pending pods per pool + cost delta estimator. I also added an alert: `gpu.pending > 5 for 3m` -> slack DM to #eng-infra and runbook link.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline — pr/5234 merged to staging: added node-probe-init DaemonSet and autoscaler policy flags. CI passed.

kai: FYI we saw a secondary issue: network MTU mismatch between instances in us-west-2a vs 2b after node reprovisioning. that caused CNI to flap and kubelet started marking pods for eviction. opened ops ticket: OPS-789.

dani: good catch — add a post-provision network check in the node-init probe (validate MTU, check CNI agent readiness) before removing `gpu-ready=false:NoSchedule`.

raj: roll plan: canary in us-west-2a (1 node), monitor pending/schedule-success for 30m, then expand to other zones. @emma can you watch the dashboard and escalate if pending > 5 or schedule_success_rate < 95%?

emma: will do. created temporary playbook notes in runbook: add step to `kubectl cordon` if we see driver install timeout > 300s. :eyes:

kai: one more: consider marking warmspares with `node.kubernetes.io/eviction-taint=soft:PreferNoSchedule` so kube-scheduler will push workload off only when necessary, and the autoscaler can prefer draining those first.

dani: agreed. we'll iterate on taint semantics: hard `NoSchedule` for unavailable nodes, soft `PreferNoSchedule` for warmspare candidate nodes, and a `soft-evict=true` annotation for best-effort pods.

raj: thanks everyone — let's monitor the canary and reconvene after 24h. /closing for now.
